target_customer: Defense primes, drone and interceptor makers and military units in Ukraine, the EU, the US and the Middle East
problem: Radar seekers for autonomous interceptors cost six figures per unit and take large teams to build, which makes them uneconomic against cheap drones.
business_model: Hardware sales of radar seekers and ground radars, with LOIs from defense customers

founders.name: Arthur Nguyen-cao
founders.background_notes: YC page cites 6+ years of RF PCB engineering. Education not listed.

founders.name: Hisham El-Halabi
education: University of Toronto, BEng Engineering Science
previous_startups: Auctify (co-founder and CTO, pivoted to Sano AI)

founders.name: Joe Gonzalez
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked on secure communications for the Navy Tomahawk fleet.

competitors.name: Cambridge Aerospace
competitors.what: Skyhammer and Starhammer interceptors using a radar seeker
competitors.traction_then: Public debut at DSEI 2025; claimed unit cost $10K to $50K, performance unvalidated publicly

competitors.name: Boeing Ultra Low-Cost Seeker
competitors.what: Low-cost seeker tested for rocket-borne tracking

technical_complexity.rationale: Miniature active radar seekers in RF PCB form at a few thousand dollars per unit require hard RF design, field testing and electronic warfare resilience; the company claims fielding in Ukraine.

defensibility.rationale: RF know-how and early battlefield data are hard to copy quickly, but primes and funded rivals are racing on low-cost seekers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Boeing and Northrop unveiled low-cost intercept tech in August 2026; no acquisition of Vernius found.

market_need_then: Shahed-class drone attacks and the US Army low-cost interceptor competition (June 2026) create demand for cheap seekers. The CEO reported $500M in non-binding LOIs and a 45-unit sale to a special forces unit, company statements not independently verified.

branding.brand_signature: Product names Archimedes and Barca; note Aurelius Systems also has a product called Archimedes
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage of the Ukraine claims by Runtime Wire and World Defense News; the CEO posted the figures on X.

brand_strength.rationale: Some niche defense press but no broader recognition and a product name clash with Aurelius.

outcome_analysis: Vernius is an active Summer 2026 company with no exit. It reports fast field testing in Ukraine, a 45-unit sale and large LOIs, helped by wartime demand for cheap interceptors and a team with RF and defense experience, but the claims are unverified and well funded rivals and primes are building low-cost seekers.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed with no investor; single aggregator, unverified, not recorded. YC page shows $580M and $500M LOI figures in different sections. The $40M Series A reported for Aurelius Systems belongs to a different company. Company page lists advisors H.R. McMaster, Austin Howard and Rob Lee as backers; amounts not stated. Completeness pass: the 125K seed rests on a single database (Dealroom) with no date or investors; searches found no press coverage of a priced round. The CEO said in replies that the company is raising (RuntimeWire, Aug 2026).
